end.summary:
Classified terminating, repeating, and non-repeating decimals.
Used repeating-decimal patterns to form fractions, including 0.1666… = 1/6.
Applied denominator factors to predict termination; correctly identified denominators with only 2 and 5 as terminating.
Recognised 1/7’s repeating block as 142857 and found 2/7 = 0.285714….
At the end, mixed up whether both 2 and 5 are required in the denominator rule; this was not corrected in the recorded lesson.
end.parentNote: Ishaan practised classifying decimals and converting repeating decimals into fractions. Their explanations using multiplication and subtraction worked well, and they identified the six-digit repeating block for 1/7. They briefly mixed up the denominator rule for 3/8; this was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, practise checking whether the reduced denominator has only factors 2 and/or 5, using examples such as 1/8, 3/20, and 7/12.
